TMQ2.question: The number of unique visitors for Amazon was more than that of Yahoo in 2020. True or False?
TMQ2.reference_chain: MAP(size(tile) → visitors) → FIND(tile[Yahoo!]) → FIND(tile[Amazon]) → CMPvis(size(tile[Yahoo!]) > size(tile[Amazon])) → ANSWER(False)
TMQ2.notes: Most participants outlined, circled or scribbled over the Yahoo! and Amazon tiles and judged area directly; a few measured width and height with arrows or estimated a ~2:1 ratio. Errors came from comparing Google instead of Amazon (2), from refusing to read area without numbers or a key (several "Impossible" or "not sure"), from one within-group share comparison (Amazon large relative to Retail), and from one participant whose overlay showed Amazon at half of Yahoo! but who still answered True.

SB100Q1.question: What percentage of Japan's Olympic medals are Bronze?
SB100Q1.reference_chain: FIND(seg[Japan,Bronze] | legend[Bronze]→color[brown], xtick[Japan]) → PROJ(bottom(seg[Japan,Bronze]) → yaxis) → READ(y)≈71 → SEG(100 − 71)≈29 → ANSWER(≈29)
SB100Q1.notes: No trial was correct. The dominant error was projecting the Japan bronze/silver boundary (~70) to the y-axis and reporting that cumulative position (69/71) instead of 100 − 71 ≈ 29. Others subtracted correctly but on the wrong bar (Australia, 48/49) or wrong segment (silver, 20), made an arithmetic slip (39), or split the bar into quarters (25). The pivotal step is SEG(top − bottom) on the correct segment.

SB100Q3.question: Which country has the highest number (absolute number, not %)  of Bronze medals?
SB100Q3.reference_chain: LOOK(ytitle[%]) → MAP(height(seg) → within-country share) → KNOW(share ≠ count without totals) → MISSING(total medals per country) → ANSWER(Impossible)
SB100Q3.notes: This is a trick item. 16 of 40 were correct, mostly by noticing the "%" in the y-axis title or reasoning that totals per country are missing. The majority bracketed or circled the large Australia bronze segment and answered Australia, treating the within-country share as a count. Several drew horizontal lines from the Australia bronze bottom across all bars to compare. Some hedgers saw the problem but still answered Australia, and a few were "correct" only because they gave up.
